title: Hopline debug frames and decision watermarking for routing observability
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: Current routing observability produces large, noisy decision traces that are expensive to store and slow to query. Teams need a compact, reconstructible representation for per-request routing paths that preserves causal order, per-hop metrics (latency/cost), and minimal artifacts needed for RCA and SLO auditing.

Goal: Implement a compact 'hopline frame' format and a decision watermarking scheme to capture a succinct per-hop snapshot for each routing decision. The solution should enable: fast console render of route paths, sampled deep-traces for debugging, and efficient long-term indexing for SLA audits.

Scope: telemetry schema, runtime capture hooks (per-hop), sampling policy, persistence format, query/index plan, console panels and developer API. Excludes full replay of request payloads and storing user-provided private data (PII).
acceptance_criteria: Define and document the hopline frame schema with fixed fields: hop_id, timestamp, chosen_node, policy_reason, latency_ms, cost_estimate_tokens, model_variant, fallback_flag, brief_context_hash
Implement runtime capture with <=1% p99 tail overhead on end-to-end request latency when sampling is off; sampled capture (1-5%) acceptable with up to 5ms additional overhead
Store compact frames in blob store with indexable metadata (request_id, customer_id, timestamp, fingerprint) and provide retention of 90 days for indexed summaries
Console rendering: per-request route path view with expandable hop frames and per-hop delta metrics; UI must load a 10-hop path within 200ms in typical region
Provide query API to fetch hopline summaries and optionally link to full trace snapshot when sampled and available
Add e2e tests and load test demonstrating storage throughput and query latency under realistic traffic
implementation_notes: Hopline frame is intentionally compact (<=512 bytes avg) to keep storage and index costs low; avoid storing full prompt/response, store a 64-bit context fingerprint instead
Watermarking: attach decision_watermark timestamps at routing start and after final hop. Watermarks allow reconstructing causal windows for sampling and correlate with KV-cache lifecycles

Sampling policy: default deterministic reservoir sampling per-customer with higher sampling for P1 customers and for requests that trigger fallback variants; allow adaptive burst sampling when error rates spike
Persistence: frames written to S3-compatible blob buckets partitioned by day and customer and a lightweight metadata record in Dynamo style index for fast lookup by request_id
Compression: use Snappy for fast decompress at console; protobuf-like binary schema to minimize size and allow forward/backward compatibility
Retention & tiering: 90-day hot index, archive to cheaper object storage after 90 days, provide unlocked audit export for enterprise customers
Privacy: strip any user tokens and do not include request bodies. Context_hash is non-reversible SHA-256 truncated to 64 bits
risks: Index growth: metadata index can grow quickly for high-volume customers — mitigated by per-customer sampling and daily partitioning
Performance overhead: naive capture can add tail latency; mitigate by async write paths and prioritized sampling
Schema drift: need careful versioning to avoid parsing issues on old console versions
Compliance: ensure no PII escapes into frames; requires review of all fields before rollout
